text:
Anya: Heads-up: RFC follow-up — canary->fallback handoff. Link: <https://redwood.internal/rfcs/handshake|rfcs/handshake>. We need a concise decision on who owns session affinity vs warmup and retry semantics. TL;DR: observer vs router ownership debate. Thoughts?
Sam: I think router should own routing/affinity policy, observer should only emit signals (quality, warmup progress). Router has the live traffic snapshot and can enforce SLOs.
Miguel: @Sam router owning affinity implies keeping staging KV/cache glue for canary sessions — that gets expensive and brittle. Alternative: observer initiates warmup on target and pushes a "handedover" marker. Tradeoffs?
Priya: Telemetry ask: include a handover_id in events so we can tie prompt/response pairs across variants for evals. Otherwise tracing is messy.
Sam: Agree on handover_id. Proposed shape: handover:{id, from_variant, to_variant, reason, seq_root}. Router can use seq_root to attempt cache mapping.
Anya: Concern: seq_root may not be stable across variants (quantized vs fp) so cache reuse could be invalid and lead to correctness bugs.
Miguel: Yep. We should split "session-warmup" (KV state) from "session-affinity". For warmup, observer should call a warmup API on the target variant and populate its cache, not ask router to clone KV.
Sam: OK. Final ownership proposal: router owns affinity/traffic switching; observer owns warmup jobs and quality signals. Router will accept a warmup_ok hook from observer before increasing traffic.
Priya: Add monitoring SLA: if warmup doesn't finish within warmup_timeout (configurable), router must fallback to previous variant and emit handover.failure metrics. Also emit handover.latency and handover.success rates.
Jared: Edge case: warmup can pass synthetic checks but still regress on long generations. Suggest a short hedging window after promotion where N% of traffic is mirrored to the old variant for sampling.
Miguel: Implementable as a sampling_window config: router mirrors a configurable sample (requests-only) to the previous variant for M seconds. Keep dual-write disabled to avoid side effects.
Anya: Sampling window + warmup timeout sounds good. Need an escape hatch: immediate manual rollback override and automated circuit if error rate spike > threshold.
Sam: Drafting an API/DSL for rollout policy. Example snippet: 
```
rollout_policy: 
  from: variant-a
  to: variant-b
  handover: 
    warmup_timeout_ms: 5000
    sampling_window_ms: 30000
    sampling_rate: 0.02
    handover_id: auto
    rollback_on_error_rate: 0.05
    observer_hooks: [warmup_start, warmup_ok, quality_signal]
```
Priya: :thumbsup: I'll add the handover_id and event schema to the telemetry spec and wire dashboards for handover.latency and sample regressions.
DeployBot: deploy-bot: canary-handoff-guardrails-v1 deployed to staging :rocket:
Sam: I'll draft the RFC appendix with the router API shapes, observer hooks, and backoff semantics. @Anya can you review the appendix before merging?
Anya: Yes. Please include a couple of concrete examples for quantized vs FP models and a short runbook for manual rollback. Meeting tomorrow 10:00 to finalize.
